whatAContractIs: The middle-end stream's frozen scope, gate and rulings. The specification is the only authority; this file records what the stream is allowed to change and what it must measure.
scope: S1 randomized semantic gate: deterministic generator of validator-clean EvoIR, differential interpretation of original versus scalar-optimized module under an explicit budget, EVP1 replay through evo-proofcheck for every trial, shrinker to a minimal reproducer. Gate: 1000 programs in the workspace test with 0 mismatches and 0 refusals; 20,000 in the ignored long run.

S1a producer binding: each rewrite binding is computed from the recorded node children (11.3), pinned by the reduced reproducer test; the seeds 1592591013 and the eleven long-run seeds replay with status 0.

S1b zero-region claim: the checker compares after.evo with the canonical rendering of the parsed before.evo (11.3); the producer emits that rendering when it admits no region; pinned by the one-instruction gapped module.
S1c fuel: E3008 is counted on its own, never as undefined behaviour (10.4).

S2 coverage and record: (S2a) extend the generator to pointers crossing block edges, data-dependent but bounded loops, copy, lifetime.end, ptr.null, func_addr with indirect calls, and multiple ordinary returns, each pinned by the coverage assertion, and re-run the 1000 and 20,000 campaigns; (S2b) the evp2 certificate version of 11.3: budget line, epoch markers, and the checker verification of 8.11 (consumed within bound, epoch markers within the declared count, stop reason consistent), with evp1 still readable. RED first for both; every campaign number from a command.

S2b restated under 1.9.36: emit evp2 with the budget line and epoch markers; the checker verifies the six properties of 11.3 Budget; evp1 stays readable and verified; the randomized gate replays evp2; a hand-written certificate for each of the six properties in its failing form is refused with status 3 and in its holding form accepted.

S2c bounded scheduler: (1) measure whether the scalar sweep is a fixpoint by re-running it on every optimized module of the 1000-program campaign and counting admitted regions; if any, the record says policy, not saturated; (2) implement the multi-epoch bounded scheduler of 8.11 (epochs until saturation or a ceiling, fuel per rule per epoch, nodes counted over the persistent graph), deterministic for a given input and budget, with truthful stop reasons; the campaigns replay with epoch markers increasing inside a block and at least one hand-constructed input that stops at each of the three ceilings; (3) the shrinker gains the merge-block-into-unique-predecessor reduction.

S2d exhaustion and telemetry: (1) the producer records saturated when its last epoch fired nothing and policy otherwise, from the scheduler's own counters; (2) on any exhaustion the certificate keeps every region admitted before the stop and the checker verifies it like any other; pinned by a test with a budget the test itself sets on the producer's own stop rule (not the profile ceilings, which stay recorded as the box); (3) the campaign table gains the residual-region count (fresh transaction over each optimized module) as a standing metric; (4) no other change.

S2e runs and coverage: (1) the run of 8.11: chain up to max_transactions = 8 transactions, stop when one admits no region, verify each certificate alone and the chain by input/output digests; the campaign reports transactions per run and residual regions after the last, which must be 0 for every run that stopped before the ceiling; (2) generator coverage: recursion (bounded by a depth argument), pointers as call arguments and return values (in-bounds by construction), copy between two distinct objects (disjoint by construction), and a shape that makes signed_shl_defined true so ub.assume.invalid_signed_left_shift is emitted; each pinned by the coverage assertion; both campaigns re-run.

S3a fact-driven rewrites (Tier B): the known-bits lattice and transfer table of 8.10 as the producer's analysis; a first Tier B rule set in a new registry revision (constant folding through facts, known-bits identities such as and(x, m) -> x when the masked bits are known, or/xor with known bits, shift by a known amount, icmp decided by known bits), each rule carrying its premise in evp2 per 11.3 Premises; the checker recomputes every premise from the region's nodes with its own implementation of the transfers and refuses a premise above the recomputed fact; the randomized gate replays; the coverage assertion names every Tier B rule as reached; a hand-edited certificate with a premise above the fact is refused (status 3). Memory rewrites stay deferred until the architect specifies them.

S3a restated under 1.9.40: producer and checker implement p0.scalar.v2 (digest c1691808ebe55a3b2520a0456345e7c38a23fa2732e0827393dcf12523024bce); the checker's transfer implementation shares no code with the producer's; every Tier B rewrite carries its premises; the campaigns replay evp2 against v2; the coverage assertion names all 18 Tier B rules; one hand-edited certificate with an unconfirmable premise is refused and one with a confirmable premise accepted; evp1 certificates against v1 stay accepted.

S3b rulings and congruence: (1) apply 1.9.41: registry order within a tier, the three dominated rules exempted in the coverage assertion as dominated, the four ratified readings pinned where not already; (2) congruence: the producer emits congruence events (7.4, 11.3 congruence lines) when two nodes become congruent through merges, the checker verifies them, and the campaigns report congruence events per transaction and regions that exist only because of one; (3) both campaigns re-run, the eight p0_009 seeds stay in the replay list.

S3c class-based matching: (1) rule matching over e-classes rather than over the instruction's own operands, so a rule fires on any node of a class that matches after congruence (common subexpressions), with the certificate recording the node the rule matched; measure regions gained and rules that now fire where they did not; (2) the shrinker gains reductions that reach the fact-bait and congruence shapes (collapse a covering mask to a constant, replace a congruent pair by one node) and re-reduces the two hand-reduced reproducers, reporting whether either gets shorter; (3) both campaigns re-run.

S3d common subexpressions and wider facts: (1) a region whose root is a duplicate of a congruent earlier node is admitted with congruence events, an extraction to the earlier node and no rewrite, so the duplicate instruction leaves the output; measure regions and instructions removed; (2) the six transfer rows added at 1.9.43 (shl, lshr, ashr, zext, sext, trunc) in both the producer's and the checker's independent implementations, the inherited negative test narrowed to what is still unlisted (division, remainder, and everything else), and a measurement of how many additional premised rewrites the new facts enable over 256 seeds with the generator baited for shifts and width changes; (3) both campaigns re-run.

S3e regions under 1.9.44: (1) eligibility, closure and manifests in both producer and checker for the six admitted operators and for structural duplicates, each recomputed independently; (2) registry p0.scalar.v3 (digest aca1f15b47e602ce18c593e06d77008862947c7c7252a9f76bb823c71f53fb15) in producer and checker, the narrowest-registry naming rule carried forward; (3) common-subexpression regions admitted (congruence events, extraction to the twin, no rewrite) with instructions removed from the output measured; (4) the six transfer rows now reachable in premises, measured on and off over 256 seeds; (5) the coverage assertion names p1_206..p1_208 and p1_230..p1_232 as reached or, if the generator cannot reach one, dominated or unreachable with the measured reason; (6) both campaigns re-run.

S3f definition-origin seeds: the producer admits regions whose seeds have origin definition per 8.7, not only entry-block arguments; both manifests recomputed independently; measure congruence-only regions (1 of 21 duplicates before), regions gained overall, and any region kind that becomes admissible; both campaigns re-run; any mismatch shrunk and pinned. A second executor takes this window with a self-contained brief.

S3g facts across block edges: (1) the seed-fact fixed point of 8.10 in the producer and, independently, in the checker, so a block argument carries the meet of the facts passed on every incoming edge; (2) premises may name seed classes and are recomputed by the checker; (3) measure, over 256 seeds and both campaigns, premised rewrites whose premise names a seed, regions gained, and the fixed point's iteration counts (distribution, maximum) as a cost figure; (4) a hand-written loop whose carried argument keeps a known mask, checked end to end through evo-proofcheck; (5) both campaigns re-run.

S3h worklist and re-derivation: the seed-fact fixed point as a worklist on both sides, bit-for-bit equal to the whole-function sweep over 256 and 20,000 seeds; the double-negation reduction re-derived against the region's partition; both campaigns re-run.

S4a policy evaluation harness (the instrument for the fourth question): a policy is (registry name, cost function, schedule parameters) behind one deterministic interface; a binary evo-policy-eval takes a policy, a corpus of EvoIR modules (generated by the randomized generator from seeds, plus the day-6/7 program corpora) and a seed, and reports per program and in aggregate: interpreter dynamic steps before and after optimization, instruction count before and after, regions, transactions, wall time, and certificate replay (must be 100 percent); it refuses any corpus path under .build/, .evidence/, or tests/contracts/day5-kernel-cohort.json and records the corpus digest in its report; two cost functions ship to prove the interface (the 7.5 default and a weighted variant), and the harness measures both over 1000 programs. No learning yet: the window ends when a policy can be swapped and its effect measured deterministically.

S4b emitting rewrites: (1) emitting right-hand sides and width_min in producer and checker per 11.6, the checker reconstructing the derived node from the pattern and bindings; (2) the checker no longer refuses on cost (11.3), pinned by a certificate whose replacement is not a default-cost improvement and is accepted, and one whose extracted root is the original node and is refused; (3) registry p0.scalar.v4 (digest 1a5391603386e18e18bfb1b2fc61985c9eb252c6e65bcb3259104bd49b2a9d74) in producer and checker; (4) the policy harness measures the three shipped cost functions over 1000 programs again: the two all-positive functions must now differ on programs containing a doubling (report how many), and the weighted function must prefer add or shl over mul by its own weights; (5) both campaigns re-run, the coverage assertion names p2_300..p2_303 as reached; (6) the day-6/day-7 corpora stay out of scope until someone inside the front-end boundary lowers them to .evo files.

S4c the first search over cost (the fourth question's first experiment): a cost function is a vector of per-operator weights (the shipped functions are points in it); a deterministic search (a fixed-seed evolutionary loop or coordinate descent, stated) over that vector on a training corpus of generated programs (seed range A) with fitness = total dynamic interpreter steps after optimization, evaluated with evo-policy-eval, 100 percent certificate replay required for every evaluated policy; the searched weighting is then measured once on a held-out corpus (seed range B, disjoint, digests recorded) against instruction-count, weighted-operators, prefer-add and prefer-shift; report steps and instructions after optimization for all five on the held-out corpus, the search's trajectory (best fitness per generation), wall time, and whether the searched weighting beats every hand-written one on held-out; the kernel cohort never enters either corpus (the harness's refusal stands); no rule changes, no schedule search yet.

B1 EvoMIR and the interpreter lane: (1) crate evocc-mir: the EvoMIR data model of docs/evomir-spec.md sections 2 to 4 with the canonical textual form of Appendix A (render and parse round-trip, byte for byte); (2) the EvoMIR interpreter with the executable semantics of section 4 (including sub-width rules of section 3), run on the same inputs as the EvoIR interpreter; (3) lowering of section 5 from extracted EvoIR to pre-allocation EvoMIR, every unsupported form refused with its section 10 code at the instruction; (4) the randomized semantic gate gains the third lane: EvoIR before, EvoIR after optimization, EvoMIR after lowering, all agreeing on results and volatile trace, with shrinking; both campaigns run with the lane; (5) no register allocation, no emission, no native run yet: that is B2 and B3. Tests first; every EvoMIR spec sentence used is cited; a gap is a SPEC_GAP stop.

B1b EvoMIR under revision 0.2: (1) every predicate row of section 5 lowered and executed, (2) results up to eight per section 6 accepted by lowering and interpreter, (3) mem.copy and frame.slot as the pseudo-forms of section 4 (replace the unrolled ldr/str copy), (4) the grammar of Appendix A round-tripped byte for byte including spelled entry labels, (5) the icmp.eq/ne extension pinned by the executor's counterexample, (6) both campaigns re-run: report lowered, refused by code, three-lane mismatches; the expectation is that refusals fall to the forms sections 5 and 10 still exclude.

B2 allocation, frame and first native run: (1) out-of-SSA per section 7 (edge copies, parallel-move resolution with x16, critical-edge splitting); (2) linear scan per section 7 with fixed operands at calls and the function boundary, spills to frame slots, deterministic tie-breaking; (3) the allocation verifier as a separate pass (definedness on every path, no two live values in one register, flags adjacency), E4020 on refusal; (4) frame layout and prologue/epilogue per section 6, ldp/stp modelled; (5) emission per section 8 for Darwin arm64: a .s file the host assembler accepts, symbols with the platform prefix, page-relative relocations; (6) the first native differential: for generated programs whose main takes no arguments and returns a bits<32>, assemble and link on the host (clang as assembler and linker, version recorded), run, and compare the exit status with the EvoIR interpreter's result over 256 seeds; then the machine lane of the randomized gate gains a fourth, native lane where the host toolchain is present; (7) the calling-convention probe of section 9 before the first cross-boundary call is emitted, and the Darwin stack-argument rule stays refused.

B2b native campaign and probe: (1) the generator mode native-main of section 9 with its own seed space (main takes no arguments, returns one bits<32>); (2) 256 seeds assembled, linked and run with the host clang, exit status modulo 256 compared with the EvoIR interpreter; any disagreement shrunk and pinned with the component named (lowering, allocation, emission, or a specification sentence); (3) the fourth lane in the randomized gate, enabled when the host toolchain is present and skipped with a counted reason otherwise, both campaigns run with it in native-main mode at 1000 and 20000 seeds; (4) the calling-convention probe of section 9: a host-compiled C program calling EvoCC-compiled functions with each admitted argument shape (1 to 8 integer and pointer arguments at every width class, one result) and the reverse, receipts naming it, before any cross-boundary call is relied on; (5) mem.copy above 64 bytes as the counted loop of section 4.

B3 the native suite and the cost of the lane: (1) the cross-boundary extension of EvoMIR 0.5 section 6 implemented and pinned by a probe shape whose host callee does not mask its own argument; (2) the four-lane 1000-seed campaign moved behind #[ignore] with a smaller default (128 seeds) in the workspace gate, since the lane costs about 25 minutes, and the 20,000-seed run measured once and reported (about three hours at the measured 0.54 s per program); (3) frames beyond the 4095-byte immediate range: a generated or hand-written program large enough to need the two-instruction form, pinned; (4) mem.copy above 65535 bytes so the counter's movz/movk sequence is exercised; (5) the C driver path end to end: a C source through the front end, the optimizer, EvoMIR, emission, the host assembler and linker, run, its exit status compared with the reference compiler's build of the same source, over the day-6 and day-7 program corpora, reporting how many of those programs the pipeline compiles and how many agree.

B4 assembly through the machine: EvoMIR carries the `asm` and `asm.goto` forms (0.6 section 4), the allocator satisfies every constraint class of 0.6 section 7 including early clobber, tied operands, address operands and register clobbers, the verifier checks them, and emission substitutes operand references and copies the template verbatim (0.6 section 8); pinned by hand-written EvoIR whose assembly the host assembler accepts and whose native run agrees with a host-compiled equivalent, one case per constraint row of EvoIR 3.11.

B5 assembly through the machine and the Linux target: (1) the B4 assembly scope already opened; (2) the narrow-result probe that settles E4014, and the result extension if the platform requires one; (3) a Linux AArch64 emission profile beside the Darwin one (symbol prefix, relocation spellings, section names), with the sealed container's GCC-14 as the differential oracle for programs that do not need libc; (4) the C corpus test moved behind a smaller default if the gate's six minutes are judged too much, the architect's call.
gate: cargo test --workspace; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo fmt --all -- --check; the 1000-program gate green; both reproducer tests green; wall time of the 1000-program test reported as the median of three runs on an idle machine.
